title: Qarlugs
capsule: The Qarluqs (Karluks) were a Turkic tribal confederation that held the Ili and Chu river valleys of Central Asia from the mid-8th century. Their political moment came at the Battle of Talas in 751, where Qarluq defection from the Tang allied force contributed decisively to the Arab Abbasid victory over Tang China, reorienting the balance of power in Transoxiana. In the following decades the Qarluqs displaced the Western Turkic Kaghanate and established dominance over much of what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Xinjiang, though they did not form a centralized state and their rulers bore the title Jabghu. By the mid-9th century Qarluq power had fragmented under pressure from Yenisei Kyrgyz expansion and internal succession conflicts, and they were gradually absorbed into successor Turkic polities including the Karakhanids.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Qarluqs' territorial footprint is poorly fixed; their loose confederation left few administrative records, and the polygon is a rough inference from Chinese, Arabic, and later Islamic sources.
